LESSON: RHYTHM

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.2: Rhythm

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Rhythm. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can various note combinations be used to form rhythms in simple time?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the effect of note extension on rhythmic patterns
2. compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 4 4 time
3. appreciate rhythmic patterns as a means of creating interest in Creative Arts and Sports

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: RHYTHM
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Rhythm helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: RHYTHM
Study Rhythm like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the effect of note extension on rhythmic patterns

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the effect of note extension on rhythmic patterns. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the effect of note extension on rhythmic patterns.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Rhythm” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the effect of note extension on rhythmic patterns. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 4 4 time

What this means
In this part you learn to compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 4 4 time. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 4 4 time.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Rhythm in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 4 4 time. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate rhythmic patterns as a means of creating interest in Creative Arts and Sports

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate rhythmic patterns as a means of creating interest in Creative Arts and Sports. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate rhythmic patterns as a means of creating interest in Creative Arts and Sports.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate rhythmic patterns as a means of creating interest in Creative Arts and Sports. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Rhythm is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Rhythm” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the effect of note extension on rhythmic patterns)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Rhythm in your own words. (skill: compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 4 4 time)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate rhythmic patterns as a means of creating interest in Creative Arts and Sports)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Rhythm to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the effect of note extension on rhythmic patterns.
3. Practise this skill: compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 4 4 time.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate rhythmic patterns as a means of creating interest in Creative Arts and Sports.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Rhythm from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Rhythm: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Rhythm?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can various note combinations be used to form rhythms in simple time?
2. How can one improvise accompaniment patterns for Sports?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Rhythm means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the effect of note extension on rhythmic patterns.
5. Be able to: compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 4 4 time.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
